native_result.query: At what Socioeconomic levels is the advantage in completion rates for Black students more pronounced?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels indicated by a positive interaction term SES*is_Black(coefficient:0.6271 (significant))
native_result.HypoB: In raw data Black students show no BA-completion advantage at any SES level: their rates are below White students everywhere, with the raw disadvantage widest at low SES (−2.6 pp in the lowest SES tercile vs −1.6 pp in the highest, Fisher p<0.001/0.026/0.144). Conditional on ability (ASVAB), class rank and sex, however, a Black advantage emerges and strengthens with SES: −1.0 pp at low SES, +1.2 pp at middle and +1.5 pp at high SES tercile (Black×SES interaction OR≈3.3, p=0.045/0.060); quartile robustness gives a monotone gradient −0.4/−0.2/+0.5/+3.1 pp, so the conditional advantage is most pronounced at the TOP of the SES distribution and absent (negative) at the bottom. Against Hispanic students Black students show no advantage at any SES level (all OR 0.59–1.13, CIs include 1).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded nls_ses_processed.csv (8773×9, no missing); 2) SES discretized into population terciles (primary) and quartiles (robustness); 3) completion rates and Black−White/Black−Hispanic gaps per bin: pp differences and Haldane–Anscombe-corrected ORs with 95% CI, Fisher exact tests; 4) logistic regressions BA ~ Black×SES_bin (+ASVAB+PERCENTILE+SEX), unadjusted vs adjusted, reported as interaction ORs and average predicted-probability differences per bin; 5) no SES×ability×race cross-tab in final results due to degenerate cells.
